## Why

The app plans trips only in the contiguous United States (functional spec sections 1 and 2). #65 told the coordinator not to offer, or add, a place outside it. But a leg between two US places can still run through Canada, since `compute_route` and the leg tools take Google's route, and no tool shows the road a route takes (technical spec 4.2). Example: the fastest drive from Detroit to Buffalo runs through Ontario, on Highway 401. The user would need a passport, and the trip would leave the area the app plans for, with nothing to tell them.

Found while working on #65, on 2026-11-04. Not seen in a recorded session yet.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 1 and 2.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 4.2, "How a waypoint is picked", and section 5.2, "Conduct".

## Open questions

- Is it worth handling at all? Few trips would cross, and the user can see the route on the itinerary view's map.
- If so, how? One way: the coordinator judges from its own knowledge of the roads whether a leg crosses the border, as it does for whether a leg reaches a must-see area, and adds a waypoint on the US side, with a reason such as "stay in the US". Another: code flags a leg whose route leaves the US, which needs the route's path, which no tool asks Google for today.

## Do

- To be settled.

- To be settled.

## Ends in

A decision, and maybe a PR.
